forecast_provider: Project model, not a NASA prediction
brief_favorable_conditions: Premontane rainforest (18–23 °C), water-filled tree holes (phytotelmata), stable humid microclimate.
why_these_variables: Temperature, dry-season rain that refills tree holes, and cloudiness (the brief cites changing cloud patterns).
absolute_value_caution: Premontane species: the NASA grid cell averages 129 m, below the habitat, so absolute temperatures are warmer. Use the change versus normal.

variables.label: Mean air temperature
variables.aggregation: Day-weighted annual mean of monthly means

variables.label: Dry-season rainfall
variables.aggregation: Annual rainfall sum over reference months [1, 2, 3, 4]; months selected using only 1981–2014, fixed for all locations.

locations.name: El Valle de Antón, regional setting

t2m_mean.model_description: Robust straight line (median of pairwise slopes), less sensitive to extreme years
t2m_mean.interval_note: Nominal 80% empirical residual band; not a calibrated guarantee. Validation windows overlap; limited residual sample.
t2m_mean.summary_text: Mean air temperature in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 26.8 °C (nominal 80% band for 2030: 26.6–27.4 °C; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 26.3 °C (+0.42 °C).

precip_dry_season.model_description: Least-squares straight line through the training years
precip_dry_season.interval_note: Nominal 80% empirical residual band; not a calibrated guarantee. Validation windows overlap; limited residual sample.
precip_dry_season.data_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.
precip_dry_season.summary_text: Dry-season rainfall in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 234.2 mm (nominal 80% band for 2030: 142.6–408.7 mm; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 144.1 mm (+90.1 mm).
